vulns.title: Unfair randomness via abort-retry on losing draws
vulns.root_cause: play is a `public fun` that draws from `&Random` and returns the payout `Coin<SUI>` to its caller. Sui already blocks the naive PTB attack: a randomness-tainted result cannot be consumed by a later PTB command, so a caller cannot inspect the draw and conditionally abort across commands. The reachable weakness is composability — because `play` is `public`, an attacker publishes a wrapper module that calls `play` and aborts inside Move whenever the returned coin is zero (a loss). Losing draws then revert for gas only while wins commit, letting the attacker extract the pool. Fix: make the randomness-consuming function a private `entry fun` (non-`public`, so no other module can wrap it) and settle the payout internally — transfer the winnings to the player rather than returning a `Coin` the caller can branch on (an `entry` return would also require `drop`, which `Coin` lacks).
